comparisons.question: Does quantum chemistry (xTB) estimate logP better than RDKit?
comparisons.finding: No. xTB performed worse than RDKit on our reference set, and the intervals do not overlap.
comparisons.decision: The pipeline uses RDKit. xTB results stay in the data download so others can check this.

a.label: Cold soak, wrung out (as in Ge Hong)

positiveControls.expected: The cold preparation ranks above the hot decoction.
positiveControls.explanation: The direction matches the historical account, but the ranges touch at 0.33. By our own pre-registered rule, touching ranges are not a clear difference, so this is borderline, not a pass.

preregistered.criterion: Positive control: cold A. annua preparation above hot decoction for artemisinin, ranges not overlapping.
xTB logP error lower than RDKit logP error on the reference set.
preregistered.detail: xTB worse; intervals do not overlap.

preregistered.criterion: Culpeper top-candidate name agreement with expert review at or above the registered threshold.
Pliny top-candidate name agreement with expert review at or above the same threshold.
preregistered.detail: Not met; source treated as lower confidence throughout.

preregistered.criterion: Top-5 hypothesis ranks stable when any one heuristic is switched off.

limitations: The model predicts extraction, not detection; plant content is not modelled.
The composition of historical wine and vinegar is unknown and modelled as ranges.
Pliny’s plant names are often disputed; results for Pliny are lower confidence.
Field extraction is AI-assisted; provisional items have not been checked by a person.
The study audit covers indexed literature only and may miss non-English work.
Heuristics (acidity, heat sensitivity) are rules of thumb.
No hypothesis has yet been tested in a laboratory.
